title: Vendor sync with conditional, delegated, and deferred items
description: Three subtleties: a conditional escalation whose trigger must be preserved (no reply by Thursday COB, then legal on Friday), a task delegated to someone not in the meeting (Dana), a decision that explicitly requires no work (logo stays) followed by a near-retraction that turns INTO a real task (FAQ line), and an explicitly deferred topic (analytics stack). Tests condition capture and decision-vs-task discrimination.

expected_tasks.name: Send final DataBridge email and escalate to legal if no reply
expected_tasks.due: email today; escalation trigger Thursday COB; legal Friday morning
key_points: final plain-language email today requesting revised renewal terms by Thursday close of business
IF no reply by Thursday COB, escalate to legal Friday morning to review termination-for-convenience options
the condition is the trigger, no further approval needed; contract lapses August 29

expected_tasks.name: Ask Dana to review the crypto sections of the security audit
expected_tasks.due: request today; Dana's assessment before the sync in two weeks
key_points: sections 4 and 6: cryptography and key management findings
Dana is on the platform team, not in this meeting; frame as a request from Ravi
if Dana lacks bandwidth, Ravi takes it to her manager

expected_tasks.name: Add the logo decision to the rebrand FAQ
key_points: one line stating the logo stays (March decision), only the color palette changes
link to the March meeting notes so the question stops recurring

acceptable_extras: the DataBridge item split into two tasks (final email; conditional legal escalation) as long as the condition is preserved

must_not_extract.reason: explicitly decided the logo stays; decision, not work
explicitly tracked by the design team already, 'nothing for this group to do'
explicitly deferred: 'a conversation for after the rebrand ships, no one touch it for now'
